title: Build, reconstruct, reload
intro: Built a quantized checkpoint pipeline and a structure-aware MLP reconstruction tool. Q converts and reloads a Qwen 4B model; R fits the output weights of a smaller Qwen 0.6B MLP and restores its saved structure. Inspect each toolchain, then its quality and runtime measurements.
qtitle: Q · A smaller checkpoint that runs
rtitle: R · Recovering output in a fixed smaller MLP
try: Try the save–reload contract on a CPU
qmethod: GPTQ converts Linear weights to packed INT4 using LLM Compressor and compressed-tensors. Activations remain BF16 (W4A16); the output head is excluded. The recorded run checks the packed artifact and the actual vLLM / Marlin execution route.
rmethod: The retained MLP channels stay fixed at zero-based layer 13. Ridge fitting uses calibration statistics in CPU FP64, solves with Cholesky, and stores the corrected down projection in BF16. The layer-aware loader restores the smaller structure from its own artifact.
qdefinition: File bytes compared with the BF16 source; a storage measurement.
memoryScope: Allocator peak includes the fixed 1 GiB KV cache and initialization/execution allocations. It is not whole-device peak memory or weight-file size.
scores: The same correct count, different probability scores
qscore: Q-BF16 is the original baseline; Q-W4 is the converted model. Each scored 137/192, with one baseline-correct answer lost and one gained. NLL measures probability on the independently computed correct token.
nllScope: Candidate minus BF16; negative is a better gold probability score. Task-balanced paired means and pointwise 95% intervals. Full-vocabulary and four-choice scores have different normalizers: one improved while the other worsened. On code, both arms always chose D, scoring 16/64; neither had an allowed label as full-vocabulary argmax on any of those 64 prompts.
qTiming: Fixed eight-token request, BF16/W4 time ratio:
timeScope: 12 fixed inputs, three process rounds; 95% interval. The interval includes 1, so these measurements do not establish a request-speed advantage.
rnames: I25 removes 25% of one MLP's channels using independent group scores; P25 uses signed pairwise interactions at the same budget. S50 is the shared 50% removal set. The suffix -R means output-weight repair. A group contains 192 adjacent channels; 16 groups form the original 3072-channel MLP.
relativeError: Mean relative output error: before → after
rScope: Relative error uses the native MLP output norm at 32 fixed positions per prompt. Energy recovery pools squared errors and is a different metric. Repair changed only down_proj.weight; tensor shapes, parameter counts and the number of inference matrices stayed fixed.
rConclusion: Local reconstruction improved in every held-out prompt, but correct counts moved in different directions. The same-size before/after request-time intervals all include 1. Inputs are short synthetic questions from shared template families; this is not a measure of recovered general model ability.
report: Read the structured report and exact definitions
fixture: A separate random tiny model demonstrates slicing, saving, process exit, directory copy and fresh CPU reload. Shape, complete outputs and tied weights are checked. It downloads no pretrained model and produces no task-quality or speed result.
routes: Choose a route: inspect recorded results, run the tiny CPU example, build a full model artifact, or reproduce the frozen study.
